page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv5 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, featuring 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations place the E32s_v5 in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with some notable strengths. The Passmark memory score is strong, ranking in the top 25% of tested systems, which aligns with its memory-optimized design. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 150.25 GB/sec for read operations and 67.0 GB/sec for write operations. In single-threaded tasks, the server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1900.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1697.0. Multi-threaded performance is supported by a Geekbench multi-core score of 14331.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 31082.87.

With its high memory density and strong memory performance, the E32s_v5 is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, in-memory caching, and data analytics. Redis SET operations reached 31.36 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput was measured at 33.78 GB/sec. For machine learning, the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation using small LLM models (321.97 tokens/sec), though it struggles with large 70B models (6.65 tokens/sec prompt processing) due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are externalized to attached Premium Storage, representing a tradeoff for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space.
